task_description: Liver toxicity (DILI) prediction. Drug-induced liver injury encompasses hepatocellular necrosis, cholestatic injury, hepatic steatosis, and mixed-pattern hepatotoxicity caused by a drug or its reactive metabolites. This task predicts whether a molecule exhibits liver toxicity, a leading cause of drug attrition and post-market withdrawal.
prediction_question: Does this molecule exhibit liver toxicity? Your final answer should be formatted as either: 'Final answer: Toxicity' or 'Final answer: Non-toxicity'.

BSEP.role: Canalicular bile salt efflux (ATP-binding cassette transporter, ABCB11)
BSEP.logic: An ATP-binding cassette transporter (ABCB11) in the hepatocyte canalicular membrane that extrudes monovalent bile salts into the bile canaliculi against a steep concentration gradient, the rate-limiting step of bile-salt secretion. Intracellular accumulation of bile salts is cytotoxic to hepatocytes, so BSEP activity keeps intrahepatic bile-salt levels low; loss of function from mutation or drug inhibition raises the intrahepatic bile-salt load and underlies progressive familial and drug-induced cholestasis.

BSEP.logic_cited: An ATP-binding cassette transporter (ABCB11) in the hepatocyte canalicular membrane[5t] that extrudes monovalent bile salts into the bile canaliculi against a steep concentration gradient[7][8t][9t], the rate-limiting step of bile-salt secretion[10t]. MRP2.role: Canalicular efflux of organic-anion conjugates and bilirubin glucuronides (ATP-binding cassette transporter, ABCC2)
MRP2.logic: A polyspecific ATP-binding cassette transporter (ABCC2) in the hepatocyte canalicular membrane that exports organic anions conjugated with glutathione, glucuronide, or sulfate, including bilirubin glucuronides, and contributes to bile-salt-independent bile flow. Loss of MRP2 function retains conjugated bilirubin and other organic anions within the hepatocyte and raises their plasma concentrations, as seen in Dubin-Johnson syndrome and in drug-induced conjugated hyperbilirubinemia.

MRP2.logic_cited: A polyspecific[15] ATP-binding cassette transporter (ABCC2) in the hepatocyte canalicular membrane[15] that exports organic anions conjugated with glutathione[15], glucuronide[15], or sulfate[15], including bilirubin glucuronides[15][16][17], and contributes to bile-salt-independent bile flow[15][18]. Loss of MRP2 function retains conjugated bilirubin and other organic anions within the hepatocyte and raises their plasma concentrations[15], as seen in Dubin-Johnson syndrome[17t] and in drug-induced conjugated hyperbilirubinemia[15][16t].

PXR.role: Transcriptional regulation of drug metabolism (nuclear receptor, not a metabolic enzyme)
PXR.logic: A ligand-activated nuclear receptor (NR1I2), not a metabolizing enzyme; on activation by xenobiotics it acts as a transcription factor. It induces expression of drug-metabolizing enzymes and canalicular efflux transporters, thereby shaping downstream hepatic drug-handling capacity.

FXR.role: Bile acid homeostasis regulation (nuclear receptor, not a metabolic enzyme)
FXR.logic: A bile-acid-activated nuclear receptor (NR1H4) that governs bile-acid homeostasis. On agonist activation it represses hepatic bile-acid synthesis and induces the bile salt export pump (BSEP), enhancing canalicular bile-salt export and lowering the intrahepatic bile-acid load.

FXR.logic_cited: A bile-acid-activated nuclear receptor (NR1H4) that governs bile-acid homeostasis[25t]. On agonist activation it represses hepatic bile-acid synthesis[26t] and induces the bile salt export pump (BSEP)[5], enhancing canalicular bile-salt export and lowering the intrahepatic bile-acid load[27].

pathway_rules: BSEP (ABCB11) provides ATP-dependent efflux of monovalent bile salts across the hepatocyte canalicular membrane; reduced BSEP activity raises intracellular bile-salt concentrations, and bile-salt accumulation is directly cytotoxic to hepatocytes.

MRP2 (ABCC2) exports glutathione, glucuronide, and sulfate conjugates and bilirubin glucuronides into the canaliculus and drives bile flow; impaired MRP2 function retains conjugated bilirubin and organic anions within the hepatocyte.

Sustained intrahepatic accumulation of bile salts and conjugated organic anions injures hepatocyte membranes and mitochondria, producing the cholestatic pattern of liver injury with associated conjugated hyperbilirubinemia.

PXR (NR1I2) is a ligand-activated nuclear receptor that, on binding xenobiotics, acts as a transcription factor inducing drug-metabolizing enzymes and canalicular efflux transporters, remodeling hepatic drug-handling capacity.

FXR (NR1H4) is a bile-acid-activated nuclear receptor that represses hepatic bile-acid synthesis and induces BSEP-mediated canalicular export, lowering the intrahepatic bile-acid load and constraining cholestatic stress.

Coordinated transcriptional control of BSEP and MRP2 by FXR and PXR sets canalicular export capacity; reduced expression of these transporters lowers biliary excretion and favors intrahepatic retention of bile salts and organic anions.

contradiction_flags.segment_text: impaired MRP2 function retains conjugated bilirubin and organic anions within the hepatocyte.
contradiction_flags.mla: Nies, Anne T., and Dietrich Keppler. "The Apical Conjugate Efflux Pump ABCC2 (MRP2)." Pflugers Archiv, vol. 453, no. 5, 2007, pp. 643-59. PubMed, https://doi.org/10.1007/s00424-006-0109-y.
contradiction_flags.contradicting_quote: Acquired or hereditary deficiency of ABCC2, the latter known as Dubin-Johnson syndrome in humans, causes an increased concentration of bilirubin glucuronosides in blood because of their efflux from hepatocytes via the basolateral ABCC3, which compensates for the deficiency in ABCC2-mediated apical efflux.
contradiction_flags.note: Basolateral export to blood is incompatible with intracellular retention; here the compensating pump is not a side note but the source's stated mechanism replacing the retention the clause asserts. The evidence is explicit for bilirubin glucuronosides, the first substrate the clause names. (Impaired MRP2 (ABCC2) function retains conjugated bilirubin and organic anions inside the hepatocyte.; In acquired or hereditary ABCC2 deficiency (Dubin-Johnson syndrome) bilirubin glucuronosides leave the hepatocyte across the basolateral membrane via ABCC3, raising their blood concentration.)

contradiction_flags.segment_text: impaired MRP2 function retains conjugated bilirubin and organic anions within the hepatocyte.
contradiction_flags.mla: Keppler, Dietrich. "The Roles of MRP2, MRP3, OATP1B1, and OATP1B3 in Conjugated Hyperbilirubinemia." Drug Metabolism and Disposition: the Biological Fate of Chemicals, vol. 42, no. 4, 2014, pp. 561-5. PubMed, https://doi.org/10.1124/dmd.113.055772.
contradiction_flags.contradicting_quote: Under pathophysiological conditions such as cholestatic liver injury and MRP2 inhibition, the basolateral efflux pump multidrug resistance protein 3 (MRP3 or ABCC3) is responsible for the occurrence of conjugated hyperbilirubinemia.
contradiction_flags.note: The clause's mechanism is hepatocellular retention; the source attributes the raised plasma conjugates to basolateral efflux, which is the opposite of retention. Upregulation of MRP3 precisely under MRP2 deficiency makes this a replacement of the mechanism, not merely a limitation of it. (Impaired MRP2 function retains conjugated bilirubin and organic anions inside the hepatocyte.; Under cholestatic injury and MRP2 inhibition the basolateral pump MRP3, strongly upregulated in MRP2 deficiency, is what produces conjugated hyperbilirubinemia, i.e. the conjugates exit the hepatocyte.)

contradiction_flags.segment_text: susceptible to oxidative S-oxidation to reactive sulfoxide, sulfenic, or sulfinic species.
contradiction_flags.mla: Henderson, Marilyn C., et al. "S-Oxygenation of the Thioether Organophosphate Insecticides Phorate and Disulfoton by Human Lung Flavin-Containing Monooxygenase 2." Biochemical Pharmacology, vol. 68, no. 5, 2004, pp. 959-67. PubMed, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bcp.2004.05.051.
contradiction_flags.contradicting_quote: MS/MS analysis confirmed the metabolites to be the respective sulfoxides. Co-incubations with glutathione did not reduce yield, suggesting they are not highly electrophilic.
contradiction_flags.note: The recorded quote EXEMPLIFIES the clause - it confirms S-oxidation to a sulfoxide - and its 'no sulfone' point concerns a species the clause never names. Only the glutathione co-incubation sentence contradicts the word 'reactive', and it does so for two thioether organophosphates with one FMO isoform. (Thioether/sulfide sulfur is susceptible to oxidative S-oxidation to REACTIVE sulfoxide, sulfenic or sulfinic species.; Expressed human FMO2.1 oxygenates the thioether of phorate and disulfoton to the sulfoxide only, and those sulfoxides did not consume glutathione, indicating they are not highly electrophilic.)
contradiction_flags.source_species: human (heterologously expressed human FMO2.1; mouse/rabbit microsomes referenced)
